description: Knechtle argues that witness reports, skeptical conversions, immediate proclamation, the empty tomb, costly adherence, and rapid church formation jointly make the resurrection historically credible.
critique: Strongest feature: As an opening constructive without reply contact, Knechtle combines witness reports, skeptical conversions, immediate proclamation, an empty tomb, costly adherence, and rapid ecclesial emergence into a cumulative inference addressing Christianity’s supernatural center. Principal limitation: The span enumerates categories without providing underlying sources, chronological corroboration, independence analysis, or a discriminating comparison demonstrating why their conjunction favors bodily resurrection over naturalistic alternatives. Live burden: Since conviction, suffering, proclamation, and institutional growth can accompany mistaken beliefs, Knechtle must establish each premise’s reliability and show that their combined pattern becomes likelier if resurrection occurred. Locked score: Seventy-four appropriately rewards a coherent, relevant constructive whose inventory engages the motion, while withholding credit because evidential foundations, comparative testing, causal linkage, and the “overnight” characterization remain underdeveloped.
